 Judgment

This is a Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ for the death of their Son Mohamed Afroz who died in a road traffic accident dated 11.04.2020.
SCCH-24 2

. The case of the Petitioners in brief is that, on 11.04.2020 at about 10.30pm, the deceased was going on Honda Activa bearing Reg.No.KA04JD5707 as a pillion rider which was ridden by one Eliyas Basha with high speed in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, in spite of repeated request made to go slow, whole so proceeding on Hosapalya - challaghatta Road, near Challaghatta Village, near BMTC Depot, due to over speed the said Honda Activa turned turtle and dashed against the road side electric pole, result of which both sustained severe injuries and Mohamed Afroz succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
3.

It is further case of the petitioners that, at the time of accident, the deceased was aged about 17 years, he was hale and healthy, studying in 10th Std., at Madarasa School, Madivala, he was very affectionate to the petitioners and the petitioners had high ambitions on the deceased SCCH-24 son.
Due to untimely sudden death of the son, both the petitioners are facing lot of mental shock, agony and financial loss.
The Kumbalagudu Police have registered a case against the rider of the Honda Activa bearing Reg.No.KA04JD5707 in Cr.No.97/2020.
After investigation, the police have filed a charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle punishable u/Sec.279, 338 and 304(A) of IPC.
The 1 st Respondent being the insurer and the 2nd Respondent being RC owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to them.
4. In response to the summons issued by this court, the Respondents have appeared and filed separate written statements.

5. The Respondent No.1 in the written statement have denied the case of the petitioners as false,
admitted issuance of policy subject to terms and conditions and SCCH-24 submitted that there is noncompliance of Section 134(C) and Section 158(6) of M.V. Act.
Further submitted that there is a delay of one day in lodging the FIR and hence it appears that the insured vehicle is falsely implicated in the case to get wrongful gains.

The rider of the insured vehicle had no valid and effective DL as on Sri.Mohamed Alam vs The New India Assurance Co on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81410874/
2 the date of the accident in contravention of policy conditions.

sentences.text: Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against them.

6. The respondent No.2 in the written statement has denied the case of the petitioners as false and submitted that his vehicle was duly insured with the first respondent and hence he is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against him.

7. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
SCCH-24 1.
Whether the Petitioners prove that, they are the legal heirs of the deceased Master Mohamed Afroz S/o Mohamed Alam.?
2. Whether the Petitioners prove that, the deceased Master Mohamed Afroz succumbed to the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 11.04.2020 at about 10.30pm near BMTC Depo.

HasapalyaChallaghatta Road,
Challaghatta Village, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru, due to the actionable negligence of the rider of the Honda Activa bearing Reg.No.KA04JD5707?

3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum?
from whom?
4.
What Order or Award?
8. In order to prove their case, the Petitioners have examined the Petitioner No.1 - Sri.Mohamed Alam who is the father of the deceased as PW.1 and got marked 11 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.11.
On the other side, the Respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf.
SCCH-24 9.
Heard arguments and perused the materials on record.

The counsel for the petitioners has filed the written arguments and also relied upon the following decisions: (i) 2021 ACJ 1146 : Chetana and Ors. Vs. Babuji M. And Ors., (ii) MFA No.6106/2017 : national Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Shashikala,
(iii) MFA 2773/2018 : Manjula Vs. Sunderraj G..
10.

Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.4 : As per final order, for the Following:

sentences.text: Issue No.2: The Petitioners to prove that the accident was occurred due the actionable negligence of the rider of the offending Honda Activa bearing No.KA04JD5707, have examined the Petitioner No.1 by name Mohammed Alam SCCH-24 i.e., the Father of the deceased as PW.1 and produced 8 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.8.
The PW.1 in his examination in chief has reiterated the averments of the petition.
On the other side, the Respondents have denied the case of the petitioners.
The respondent No.1/Insurer has not examined any witness including the eye witness who had witnessed the accident or produced any documents.

In the crossexamination of PW.1 it is elicited that, they have not produced any documents to prove that the age of the deceased and also not produced any documents to prove that the deceased was studying in Madarasa, he also not knows the name of the Madrasa in which the deceased was studying.
Except this nothing worth is elicited to disprove the alleged manner of accident and non involvement of the insured vehicle.

12. Further, the FIR, FIS, spot mahazar, spot sketch, MVA report, inquest mahazar, PM report,
charge sheet as per Exs.P.1 to P.8 are public documents which SCCH-24 have got presumptive value under law.
As such, there are no reasons to discard the evidence of PW.1 and the documents produced by the PW.1 and accept the version of Respondent No.1.

Under these circumstances,
relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with documents produced by him, this court is of the opinion that, the driver of the offending vehicle had ridden it in a rash and negligent manner,
endangering to human life and made it to turtle and dashed against road side electric pole, result of which deceased had sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to injuries.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is held in the affirmative.
13. Issue Nos.1 and 3:
It is the case of the Petitioners that, the Petitioner No.1 is the Father and the Petitioner No.2 is the Mother of the deceased - Mohamed Afroz.
To prove this relationship, the PW.1 has entered into witness box and specifically deposed this relationship in his chiefexamination on oath.
SCCH-24
Apart from that, the Petitioners have also produced their Adhar Cards and also Adhar Card of the deceased as per Exs.P.9 and P.11.
They have also produced PM report as per Ex.P.8, in which the name of the petitioner No.1 is mentioned showing him as father of the deceased.
In Ex.P.11 the name of the father of the deceased is mentioned as Mohammed Alam who is the petitioner No.1 in this case.

These documents are public documents which have got presumptive value under law and have not been seriously disputed by the Respondents and no contrary admission is obtained in the cross examination of PW.1.
The Respondent No.2 have not produced any contrary evidence on record.
As such, there are no reasons to discard these documents produced by the Petitioners.

Under such circumstances, relying upon the oral and documentary evidence of the Petitioners, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioners have proved the relationship with the deceased that the Petitioner No.1 is SCCH-24 the Father and the Petitioner No.2 is the Mother of the deceased - Mohamed Afroz.
14. While discussing the issue No.2, this Tribunal has come to the conclusion that the due to actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle the alleged accident occurred.

Therefore,
under these circumstances, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation.

sentences.text:
Age of the deceased:
15.
In so far as age of the deceased is concerned, the Petitioners have produced the Aadhar Card as per Ex.P.11.
As per this document his date of birth is 01.01.2003 and the accident was occurred on 11.04.2020.
As such the deceased was 17 years as on the date of accident and from this, it is very clear that as on the date of accident, the deceased was a minor.
Since the deceased was minor as on the date of accident, it shall be deemed that he was not working and not earning anything.

As per the case of the SCCH-24 petitioners the deceased was studying in Madrasa and was a bright student but have not produced single document in this regard and hence the said claim of the petitioners that deceased was studying in Madrasa is not acceptable one.

Further the counsel for the petitioners has relied above the three decisions which are referred above and argued that the notional income charge of KSLSA be considered while fixing the income of the deceased and future prospects be awarded.

I have perused the said decisions and in the the Hon'ble H.C. clearly observed that the deceased therein was student and doing milk vending but in this case no single document is placed on record to prove that the deceased was studying in Madarasa and even the PW.1 clearly stated that he does not know the name of the Madarasa, this itself is sufficient to hold that the deceased was not studying and hence the said decisions are not applicable to the SCCH-24 present case as the facts and circumstances are different.
16. Now the quantum of compensation needs to be considered.
The counsel for the petitioners submits that the decision rendered in Sarla Verma's case needs to be considered and the said multiplier is applicable to the age of the deceased.

With great respect to the said decision this Tribunal is of the view that 'the multiplier held in the said decision with regard to earning members and hence as in this case the deceased is considered as nonearning member and hence the said decision is not applicable to fixing multiplier to the age of the deceased of this case.
Therefore, the decision in the case of 'KISHAN GOPAL AND ANR. VS. LALA AND ORS.' rendered by Division Bench of Hon'ble Supreme court is aptly applicable to this case.

entities.text: KISHAN GOPAL AND ANR. VS. LALA AND ORS
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In order to ascertain the quantum of compensation to the minors nonearning SCCH-24 members, the decision of the Hon'ble supreme court reported in Kishan Gopal Vs. Lala 2013 SCW 5037 wherein it is held that in case of death of minors, yearly notional income has to be considered at Rs.30,000/ per annum and the age of the youngest parent of the deceased has to be considered for multiplier.
As per Ex.P.9 - Aadhar Card of the mother of the deceased by name Samina Khatoon (Petitioner No.2) her date of birth is 01.01.1974.
The accident occurred on 11.04.2020.
So, as on the date of accident the age of mother of the deceased was 46 years.
Therefore the proper multiplier applicable to her age is 13.
Therefore, the total loss of dependency would be Rs.3,90,000/ (Rs.30,000/ X 13 = Rs.3,90,000/).
The Petitioners have claimed that they have spent Rs.75,000/ towards transportation of dead body and towards funeral obsequies.
In this regard they have not produced any documents to show the expenses.
However, looking into the facts and SCCH-24 circumstances of the case, it would be appropriate to award compensation of Rs.20,000/ towards funeral and transportation expenses.
If the deceased was alive certainly he would have saved some amount out of his earnings and created estate in favour of the Petitioners.
Therefore, a sum of Rs.20,000/ is awarded under the head of loss to the estate.

Further, relying on the decision in Magma General Insurance company Limited wherein the Hon'ble Apex court has considered the compensation under head of loss of consortium and further The Hon'ble Apex court in three Judge Bench in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd.

5 Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2020) SCC online 410, had reaffirmed the view of the two judge Bench in Magma General Insurance company Ltd.

Therefore, the claimants are also entitled for compensation under the head of filial consortium of Rs.80,000/ (Rs.40,000/
SCCH-24 each).

As such, in total the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.5,10,000/
alongwith interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petitioner till deposit.

LIABILITY:
17.
The Respondent No.1 have not lead any evidence and not proved their defence.
Therefore the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
As the policy existed and hence the respondent No.1 is to indemnify the 2nd respondent and directed to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The Petitioners claimed an amount of Rs.30,00,000/ but they are entitled only for a sum of Rs.5,10,000/.
Hence, the petition is liable to decreed/allowed in part.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is in the affirmative and Issue No.3 is partly in the affirmative.
18. Issue No.4:

In view of the findings on the above issue Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:
SCCH-24 ORDER
The Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with cost.

The Petitioners are entitled for Compensation of Rs.5,10,000/ (Rupees Five Lakhs and Ten Thousand only) alongwith interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of Petition, till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondents 1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.1/Insurance company is directed to deposit the award amount and interest before this Tribunal within 60 days from the date of this Judgement.
SCCH-24

On deposit of the award amount and interest, 15% shall be deposited in the name of the Petitioner No.2 for a period of 3 years in any Nationalized or scheduled bank and balance shall be released to both the Petitioners equally on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules

. 
The Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1000/.
Draw Award accordingly.

(Miss. ANNAPOORNESHWARI) C/c XXII Addl. Small Causes Judge, Bangalore.
